findings: CheckMode is a sealed 2-variant enum (ReportOnly/Blocker) — zero runtime deps added. Derives Clone+Copy+Debug+Default+Eq+PartialEq matching the ViolationKind pattern already in oya-check-statelessness.
Default=ReportOnly expresses the correct safe default: early substrate phases never block CI unintentionally.
is_blocker() predicate avoids boolean-matching call-sites; matches!() macro used cleanly.
Display impl ('report-only'/'blocker') matches the --report-only/--blocker CLI flag names from the plan spec exactly.
CheckMode carries zero runtime cost: Copy enum with a single bool predicate. No allocations, no locks, no I/O.
Both variants are stateless and trivially serializable; compatible with any scale-out CI runner topology.
Default=ReportOnly ensures hyperscaler-grade safety: gates never accidentally block distributed pipelines before lanes are fully wired.
No external inputs accepted: CheckMode is constructed only from CLI flag parsing under caller control.
No unsafe code; #![forbid(unsafe_code)] inherited at crate level — no memory-safety attack surface.
Blocker variant can only tighten (not loosen) gate behavior; no privilege escalation possible.
is_blocker() predicate gives a clear call-site idiom: if mode.is_blocker() { return Err(...) }.
Default=ReportOnly means zero-arg construction produces the safe passive mode; opt-in to blocking is explicit.
Display impl mirrors CLI flag strings verbatim, making log output self-documenting.
3 unit tests per crate: default variant, blocker predicate, Display output. 26/26 green including all 20 pre-existing tests.
ADR-0083 Tier-3 cfg_attr exemption already present in both crates; no new allowances needed.
Zero new dependencies in either Cargo.toml.
Alternative A (bool flag): rejected — bool parameters have no self-documenting variant names; CheckMode enum is more legible at call sites.
Alternative B (new crate oya-check-mode): rejected — single 2-variant enum does not warrant a standalone crate; merge-into-existing-crates is the minimum viable approach per user-directive-option-2.
Alternative C (feature flag): rejected — runtime enum is more flexible and testable than compile-time features for CI gate behavior.
No secrets, credentials, or PII involved; enum is a pure discriminant type.
No network I/O, file I/O, or subprocess execution in CheckMode itself.
Blocker mode cannot be coerced to ReportOnly by downstream code — Default is ReportOnly but callers must explicitly construct Blocker; no confused-deputy risk.
No data-class fields introduced (enum is discriminant-only).
No unsafe code; #![forbid(unsafe_code)] inherited at crate level.
